summary: A pot is set on the fire and filled with water and meat. The same spelling also names a thorn, and Ecclesiastes plays on the sound of thorns crackling beneath a pot.

senses.definition: Elisha tells his servant to set the large pot on to boil stew. A psalm pictures thorn fuel under cooking pots and calls Moab a basin for washing.
Thorn bushes grow among the ruins of Edom. Ecclesiastes compares a fool’s laughter to thorns crackling under a pot. The hooks in Amos are used to haul people away.

note: The indexing groups the vessel with סחר, travel and trade. Neither the form nor the passages show that derivation. The verse in Ecclesiastes deliberately brings the two nouns together.
